headline: Highest risk is medium: plano’s broad egress can leak or misroute marker-derived content, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict paths are mostly blocked by marker’s no-write/no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem read/write, no browser, no subprocesses, and no MCP, so it cannot ingest plano output by default. Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and file config, but there is no shared channel or parser bridge documented between them. The interaction is therefore provably blocked on the marker side.
conditions: IF marker gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge to plano, reassess as non-none.
IF plano output is manually copied into marker prompts, prompt-injection risk becomes user-mediated.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not add a shared clipboard or message queue.
Disable any future MCP bridge between them.
Review copied text before pasting into marker.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. Plano has broad network egress and handles logs/metrics/traces, but the pair lacks a documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow. The remaining pathway is limited to unusual operator-created sharing, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace, leakage risk rises.
IF marker is configured to read user documents that plano also exports, data can cross between them.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent.
Do not mount the same directory into both runtimes.
Restrict plano egress to approved endpoints.
Avoid placing secrets in plano logs or traces.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Plano also lacks subprocesses and does not advertise filesystem write or git mutation. With no overlapping write surface, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, reassess for conflict.
IF git or database mutation is added to plano, locking should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Do not grant git write permissions to either agent.
Use separate config files per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs may be treated as facts by downstream systems. Plano is a travel-planning/gateway agent with broad egress, so if it consumes marker output without verification, errors can cascade into external actions or routed requests. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF plano uses marker output as authoritative input without validation, cascading error risk is active.
IF marker-generated text is forwarded into API calls or travel decisions, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before plano acts.
Require schema validation on marker output.
Compare marker output against a second source.
Log provenance for every forwarded field.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before actioning outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, and marker has no network egress. Plano does handle logs/metrics/traces and broad egress, which can create retention or residency issues if sensitive data is introduced, but the profiles do not show a default compliance mismatch. Only plano is cited because the risk is one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through plano logs or traces, compliance review is required.
IF marker is used on regulated documents and outputs are forwarded to plano, retention policy alignment must be checked.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to plano by default.
Set short retention on plano logs.
Redact identifiers before forwarding outputs.
Document data residency for any shared workflow.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
